decisions.title: CBongo/game-music-extraction

decisions.title: ajoneil/morepork
decisions.reason: Primary documentation establishes reusable execution-trace capture, query, comparison and visualization across five legacy emulator families, directly supporting software archaeology.

decisions.title: amypurple/AmyStudio
decisions.reason: Primary documentation establishes a runnable browser-based ColecoVision development environment with its own Z80-oriented language, compiler, assembler, runtime, examples and embedded test/debug emulator.

decisions.title: plasticbugs/mrdoarcade
decisions.reason: Primary README and shared assembly source establish a substantial ColecoVision fan conversion built from a documented Captain Cosmos disassembly, with five reproducible ROM variants and real-hardware/emulator use.

decisions.title: mstan/SuperMarioBrosNESRecomp
decisions.reason: Fully playable native title port with documented all-world coverage and a bounded demo nondeterminism caveat.

decisions.title: mstan/DuckHuntNESRecomp
decisions.reason: Playable native title port with a documented mouse-backed Zapper implementation.

decisions.title: mstan/DrMarioNesRecomp
decisions.reason: Playable native title port with explicitly bounded one-player and regional-ROM validation.

decisions.title: mstan/LegendOfZeldaNESRecomp
decisions.reason: Independently runnable native title port with explicit overworld, dungeon and missing-dispatch validation.

decisions.title: mstan/FaxanaduRecomp
decisions.reason: Independently runnable native title port tested from title screen through credits, without overstating exhaustive coverage.

decisions.title: mstan/YoshiNESRecomp
decisions.reason: Independently runnable native title port with documented one-player, two-player and demo coverage.

decisions.title: mstan/YoshisCookieRecomp
decisions.reason: Independently runnable native title port with one-player and versus testing plus zero-divergence oracle comparison against Nestopia.

decisions.title: mstan/Megaman3NESRecomp

decisions.title: mstan/GumshoeNESRecomp

decisions.title: drhelius/Gearsystem
decisions.reason: Fresh SG-1000/SC-3000 code search resolved to the already indexed Gearsystem emulator/debugger record; it is not a new project.

decisions.title: drhelius/Gearcoleco
decisions.reason: Fresh ColecoVision code search resolved to the already indexed Gearcoleco emulator/debugger record; it is not a new project.

decisions.title: ocornut/meka
decisions.reason: Fresh Sega 8-bit/ColecoVision code search resolved to the already indexed MEKA emulator record; it is not a new project.

decisions.title: Adventure — SourceGen conversion
decisions.reason: The author states this is a conversion of Joel D. Park's existing commented disassembly and adds essentially no new analysis; do not count the conversion as an independent reverse-engineering project.

decisions.title: Super Mario Bros. — SourceGen conversion
decisions.reason: The author ports doppelganger's existing disassembly and says he has not meaningfully modified the original analysis. Pattern-table visualizers are useful but this is not a separate original game disassembly.

decisions.title: Applesoft BASIC — SourceGen conversion
decisions.reason: The ROM collection identifies this as a conversion of Bob Sander-Cederlof's pre-existing S-C Documentor disassembly; the converted listing is not counted separately. His underlying work remains a potential independent lead.

decisions.title: Super Serial Card firmware — manual conversion
decisions.reason: The ROM index explicitly describes the SourceGen SSC listing as ported from Apple's published firmware source in the installation manual, rather than a separate reconstruction.

decisions.title: Selected Apple II monitor ROMs — published-listing conversions
decisions.reason: The original, autostart, unenhanced IIe and original 16KB IIc monitor listings are described as faithful SourceGen reproductions of published Apple sources with little added commentary. This does not cover James Lewis's expanded 32KB IIc work, independent monitor analysis elsewhere, or James Davis's separate full-ROM project.

decisions.title: Apple IIe 80-column firmware — manual conversion
decisions.reason: The listing says its labels and comments come from Apple's published 80-Column Firmware Listing and describes itself as a fairly direct translation, so this SourceGen copy is not a separate original disassembly.

decisions.title: Apple II DOS 3.3 original-source archive
decisions.reason: Listed under original source listings in the SourceGen outbound index. The repository preserves original DOS 3.3 source and reference material; inspect its own annotations before claiming a distinct reverse-engineering project.

decisions.title: Robotron: 2084 (Atari 7800) — imported disassembly
decisions.reason: The listing's header attributes the Atari 7800 disassembly to Dan Boris with additional work by Scott T, while the enclosing repository documents a separate Apple II Robotron project. Resolve the credited original author's current source before cataloguing a canonical Atari 7800 research record.

decisions.title: jotd666/berzerk
decisions.reason: The sole Berzerk Z80 listing credits Scott Tunstall as its reverser, and the fuller canonical ScottTunstall/Berzerk repository is available. JOTD’s copied file has no independently evidenced Amiga translation; follow the original author for this arcade analysis.

decisions.title: jotd666/super_pacman
decisions.reason: Project-specific 6809 disassembly qualifies as arcade analysis. The README describes Mappy and the Amiga makefile references a missing super_pacman.68k, so no Super Pac-Man Amiga port or working build is claimed.

decisions.title: jotd666/digdug
decisions.reason: Copied Dig Dug II README is superseded by the game-specific Dig Dug Z80 listing and Amiga assembly, with build/playability still unknown.

decisions.title: jotd666/rolling_thunder
decisions.reason: Copied Jail Break README does not describe this repository, but dual 6809/MCU listings, a distinct Rolling Thunder Amiga driver and TODO justify a work-in-progress record without build or playability claims.

decisions.title: jotd666/tiger_heli
decisions.reason: Project-specific Z80 disassembly qualifies as arcade analysis. README describes Jail Break, Amiga code describes Commando and makefile Dig Dug 2; no Tiger Heli Amiga port is claimed.

decisions.title: jotd666/bosconian
decisions.reason: Copied Rally-X README is superseded by Bosconian Z80 listing and Bosconian-specific Amiga driver work; no playable port claim.

decisions.title: jotd666/mrdo
decisions.reason: Copied Jail Break README is superseded by Mr. Do! Z80 listing and Amiga-specific sprite/high-score code; predecessor template remains acknowledged.

decisions.title: jotd666/jungle_king
decisions.reason: A 256 KB Z80 listing and post-processing script qualify as an arcade disassembly; repository has no Amiga code, so an Amiga conversion is not claimed.

decisions.title: jotd666/jrpacman500
decisions.reason: The 15 KB screenshot-to-68000-data conversion script is concrete Amiga development tooling, but the repository has only an assets directory and no generated src tree, game source or working build.

decisions.title: jotd666/marble_madness_2
decisions.reason: A 27 KB C RAM-dump renderer and graphics conversion script qualify as arcade video analysis. The Amiga slave and TODO lack completed ROM patching and tile/sprite ripping, so the record does not claim a playable Amiga port.

decisions.title: jotd666/amitools
decisions.reason: Fork of existing Amiga tools; no distinct JOTD reverse-engineering work established.

decisions.title: jotd666/mame
decisions.reason: MAME fork; no standalone Amiga/ST reconstruction demonstrated.

decisions.title: jotd666/Musashi
decisions.reason: 68000 emulator fork; review upstream rather than cataloguing an unverified duplicate.

decisions.title: jotd666/musashi040
decisions.reason: 68000 emulator fork; review upstream rather than cataloguing an unverified duplicate.

decisions.title: jotd666/gods-deluxe
decisions.reason: Primary Gods Deluxe README documents a substantial beta behavioral remake of the Amiga/Sega game, including observed differences and incomplete level coverage.

decisions.title: jotd666/supercars3
decisions.reason: Project readme.txt documents a substantial playable Super Cars I/II remake and original circuits with known AI/physics differences.

decisions.title: jotd666/pbmplus
decisions.reason: General image utility suite, not a distinct Amiga/ST reverse-engineering target.

decisions.title: jotd666/misctools
decisions.reason: README describes general-purpose Python home/work command-line scripts; grepbin alone does not establish a distinct Amiga/ST research project.

decisions.title: BLACK ICE — original Atari STE game
decisions.reason: Project-specific README explicitly says BLACK ICE is original homebrew built using lessons from the workspace, not a reconstruction or reverse-engineering project. Its Hatari-tested 1 MB STE target is useful development context but does not warrant a catalogue entry.

decisions.title: Into The Eagle’s Nest — misattributed Amiga/Atari ST entry
decisions.reason: The second catalogue entry described this same repository as a partial Amiga/Atari ST reconstruction. Its README and 68000 source establish only an Amiga disassembly. Merged the duplicate into the existing Amiga record and removed the unsupported Atari ST attribution.

decisions.title: The Air Dirt Demo
decisions.reason: README identifies full original assembler source for the group’s own 1996 Falcon demo, with no binary-to-source recovery claim.

decisions.title: The Ultimate Fake
decisions.reason: README identifies full assembler source for the group’s own 1998 ST demo; original-source publication does not itself establish reconstruction.

decisions.title: Xmas Card 97
decisions.reason: README identifies full assembler source for the group’s own 1997 Falcon demo, without a disassembly/reconstruction claim.

decisions.title: ST Floormat
decisions.reason: README identifies the original source and an old source version of the group’s own demo; the Falcon hardware requirement is not evidence of reverse engineering.

decisions.title: Dadplazz
decisions.reason: README identifies full original Falcon demo source and documented build instructions; no binary-to-source reconstruction is described.

decisions.title: RAWTex — planned Amiga/ST planar support
decisions.reason: README says Amiga and Atari ST planar export is planned, while current indexed chunky output primarily targets other architectures; revisit if support lands.

decisions.title: ProTrekkr
decisions.reason: Maintained modern music tracker and heavily modified NoiseTrekker derivative, but README does not establish a distinct Amiga/ST reverse-engineering subject or core disassembly/debugging tool.

decisions.title: STTRANS Atari ST-Book transfer research
decisions.reason: Original STTRANS.PRG, Ghidra project and substantive Python serial companion provide concrete STBook transfer protocol work; no reconstructed executable is claimed.

decisions.title: Starflight Atari ST analysis
decisions.reason: Ghidra project and BTX, AGO and OMEGA Python asset readers substantiate Atari ST binary and format analysis, without claiming a playable Starflight rebuild.

decisions.title: Think & Work Atari ST original-source port
decisions.reason: Author explicitly describes writing this Atari ST game from scratch from the Atari XL game levels and publishing its own original 68k source. No reverse-engineered binary or recovered-source work is established.

decisions.title: TurboAss Atari ST assembler original source
decisions.reason: Publishes the author’s original Atari ST assembler, editor and debugger source rather than independent recovery of a binary or a reconstructed legacy codebase.

decisions.title: AtariDocumentation official manual conversions
decisions.reason: Transcriptions and OCR/text conversions of Atari documentation. This is a document source archive rather than an independent software reverse-engineering subject.

decisions.title: Atari_ST_Sources original-source archive
decisions.reason: Large collection of existing Atari ST assembly and C source trees. The archive alone does not establish a distinct binary-to-source reconstruction project; review a specific contained project separately if authored reverse-engineering evidence appears.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/4489_byteloader
decisions.reason: GitHub identifies this as a fork of 4489/4489_byteloader; copied README credits upstream and does not establish a separately documented disassembly. The Infinite Dreams README cites this loader in its later single-disk adaptation.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/amigaprogramming
decisions.reason: Original Amiga 68000 programming examples, without a documented recovered historic binary or reverse-engineered target.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/TTEDiskBuilder-netcore
decisions.reason: README identifies a .NET Core port of h0ffman’s existing ADF disk builder for VS Code; a useful development utility, but no separate reconstructed historical format or subject analysis is demonstrated.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/modprocessor
decisions.reason: Modern ProTracker sample recompression experiment for the author’s demo adaptation; README describes an untested original support utility, not a historic binary or format reconstruction.

decisions.title: MarkyTurtle/HardwareKeyboardReader
decisions.reason: README describes new Amiga 500 hardware keyboard library code and an in-progress VS Code example, not a reverse-engineered legacy software subject.

decisions.title: Championship Manager 93 folder
decisions.reason: Championship Manager 93 folder contains a game executable/data and patched binary but no distinct source reconstruction or analysis code. The documented Italia reconstruction is already catalogued; a second project for this binary folder would misstate its evidence.

decisions.title: DELA Eprommer reverse engineering
decisions.reason: Primary work reconstructs an Amiga expansion peripheral circuit and PAL equations, while its CLI is newly written to operate that hardware. It does not reconstruct legacy software within the tracker’s software-archaeology scope.

decisions.title: Tearaway Thomas partial reimplementation
decisions.reason: Packed/unpacked dumps and the Python DHp2 unpacker substantiate Amiga game data analysis; broader playability or full game reconstruction is not claimed.

decisions.title: cyxx/another_js
decisions.reason: The browser engine interprets Another World VM opcodes with DOS game data; promoted under DOS origin. Its Amiga palette option alone does not establish Amiga disk compatibility.

decisions.title: cyxx/hode
decisions.reason: A substantial Heart of Darkness engine reimplementation uses Windows demo/CD resource files; promoted under the Windows source platform without an Amiga or Atari ST claim.

decisions.title: nitecrwl
decisions.reason: Author labels the Atari ST game decompiled; gameplay C++, GEM AES/VDI code and cross-build Makefile substantiate source recovery. Original binary identity, matching and runtime verification remain unknown.

decisions.title: amiga_reconstructed
decisions.reason: Three named Amiga intros/trainers from this collection are already catalogued. Remaining directories have not been individually matched to a specific binary or reviewed for distinct reconstruction code; defer only those unexamined components rather than the entire collection.

decisions.title: amigaos-kickstart-source-history
decisions.reason: Surviving original AmigaOS RCS revisions were restored into a browsable Git timeline. This is source-history restoration within the preservation scope; it is not a ROM-derived reconstruction. Version tags and chronology are approximate.

decisions.title: ActionReplayAmiga
decisions.reason: Reverse engineered Action Replay hardware schematics and PAL/FPGA plans; hardware analysis rather than software or firmware reconstruction for the catalogue.

decisions.title: MidiMaze2
decisions.reason: Repository README offers historical shareware archives, disk images and screenshots, without source reconstruction or RE work in the repository.

decisions.title: STOS
decisions.reason: Original and adapted STOS BASIC interpreter/compiler assembly trees qualify as historical Atari ST development tooling. No binary-derived reconstruction or verified modern end-to-end build is claimed; component provenance remains open.

decisions.title: Amberstar original-source archive
decisions.reason: Original incomplete tokenized GFA Assembler development source archive, per its README. Preserve as provenance for Amberstar without treating it as a reverse-engineered reconstruction.

decisions.title: Boulder Dash modern Amiga clone
decisions.reason: New Amiga clone with editor; no primary evidence of recovered code or historical file-format analysis.

decisions.title: Pushover browser port (DOS-derived)
decisions.reason: Static and DOSBox analysis of Pushover DOS executables produced a browser game recreation using DOS data; promoted under DOS origin without asserting Amiga/ST binary or asset analysis.

decisions.title: The Faery Tale Adventure original Amiga sources
decisions.reason: Repository explicitly publishes original Amiga Aztec C/68000 source rather than a reverse-engineered reconstruction. Valuable historical source archive, but outside a distinct RE record.

decisions.title: Exploring Another World — DOS data research
decisions.reason: Concrete Haskell MEMLIST.BIN and BANK parsers qualify as DOS resource analysis. Referencing an Amiga ADF as background does not demonstrate decoding it.

decisions.title: Rockford Patcher — DOS target
decisions.reason: The patcher changes PC Rockford executable and data to recover hidden levels; promoted under DOS only. Historical Amiga art comparisons do not demonstrate Amiga binary patching.

decisions.title: L-Packer — source pending
decisions.reason: Documented and distributed beta packs Amiga and Atari ST executables, qualifying as directly relevant development tooling. Source is promised for a later release and is absent now; source audit and reproducible build are unknown.

decisions.title: Amiga smbfs — upstream protocol reverse engineering
decisions.reason: Amiga SMBFS is a port of Sharity-Light SMB filesystem code. The cited reverse engineering concerns SMB network protocol behavior, while this repository does not analyze a retro Amiga disk, application, executable, or game format; an ordinary native filesystem port alone falls outside the catalogue’s archaeology/tooling scope.

decisions.title: A2232 firmware historical source archive
decisions.reason: Archive contains original Commodore-era sources, including A2232 card firmware, rather than a reconstructed binary or new analysis project.

decisions.title: image-rider STX parser
decisions.reason: The example can extract STX track and sector data and the source implements parser scaffolding. README says formats are not fully parsed; included strictly as exploratory STX tooling.

decisions.title: FujiBoink Amiga conversion
decisions.reason: Atari ST demo to Amiga conversion includes Amiga assembly and asset-generation scripts. Included as a native port, without a binary-derived decompilation claim.

decisions.title: glfrontier FrontierVM 3
decisions.reason: FrontierVM 3 is a later experimental OpenGL renderer in Tom Morton’s existing FrontierVM/Atari ST Frontier lineage, already catalogued as frontier-vm-atari-st. External fe2.s game data and an incomplete renderer limit playability, but neither is a reason to defer a separate discovery decision.

decisions.title: albank1 Agent USA
decisions.reason: The collection lists Agent USA in its README but the tree contains only agentusa.prg, with no Agent USA assembly listing, parser or analysis source to catalogue as an independent reconstruction.

decisions.title: mist64/c64ref
decisions.reason: A curated reference collection and web presentation of ROM listings/memory maps by multiple historical authors. No distinct new binary reconstruction or original parser is established for this repository; the separately buildable c64rom project is catalogued.

decisions.title: Pokefinder-org/final_cartridge_3_original
decisions.reason: GitHub identifies this repository as a fork of mist64/final_cartridge, the canonical reconstructed cartridge source added in this batch; no separately evidenced original work was identified.

decisions.title: unorig/DrWhoandtheMinesofTerror
decisions.reason: Repository currently contains only a Markdown item list; the description claims reverse-engineered C64 code, but no source, parser, or reproducible analysis artifact is present.

decisions.title: Piddewitt/C64-Game-Source-Code
decisions.reason: This repository is an index README linking the author’s separate game repositories, with no game source tree of its own; the linked original game studies are already catalogued individually.

decisions.title: g0me3/fceux
decisions.reason: This is a fork of TASEmulators/fceux described only as an Oregon Trail emulator. The current repository description does not establish whether it contains a distinct debugging, analysis or preservation contribution; compare the fork diff and locate project-specific documentation before deciding whether it warrants an independent record.

decisions.title: Crossroads II — old hyphz link
decisions.reason: The January 2025 article cites this old GitHub path; GitHub resolves the repository to MarkRdgOx/crossroads-2-disassembly, already tracked as crossroads2-c64-markrdgox.

decisions.title: Populous C/SDL2 fork
decisions.reason: Fork adds partial C translation but couples it to a game-specific SDL2 Amiga hardware layer, and many game routines remain stubs. Execution boundaries and distinct usable output need an audit before any promotion under the current game-specific-emulation exclusion.

decisions.title: AMSDOS ROM listing in Amstrad-ROM-Sources
decisions.reason: The directory README says the author's own initial work was abandoned and the completed disassembly is an unidentified predecessor's work copied for discoverability; no distinct analysis by this repository is demonstrated for AMSDOS.

decisions.title: GuillianSeed/MetalGear
decisions.reason: Primary documentation establishes a fully annotated MSX2 disassembly and reproducible Japanese/English ROM builds with expected CRC32 values.

decisions.title: mcolom/arkanoid_msx_disasm
decisions.reason: The annotated source documents z80dasm provenance, a z80asm rebuild command and the expected rebuilt-ROM SHA-1.

decisions.title: ValleyBell/PC98VNResearch
decisions.reason: The collection provides original PC-98 engine/game format research, tools, IDA material and rendered 16-bit x86 disassemblies rather than only links or binary assets.

decisions.title: FuzionCD/lime-juice
decisions.reason: Current C++ compiler/decompiler and image round-trip suite provides substantive PC-98 bytecode/data archaeology tooling with explicit supported and unsupported boundaries.

decisions.title: tomyun/juice
decisions.reason: lime-juice explicitly identifies this Racket implementation as its predecessor and carries the same Juice MES-tool lineage forward; it is retained as relationship evidence rather than a second catalogue record.

decisions.title: nmlgc/ReC98
decisions.reason: Primary documentation describes a maintained source reconstruction of Touhou 1–5 whose rebuilt PC-98 executables remain bit-perfect on every commit.

decisions.title: nmlgc/np2debug
decisions.reason: This Neko Project II fork documents a substantial debugger feature set built specifically for modification and translation of PC-98 binaries.

decisions.title: sidneycadot/Atari8bit_OSB-NTSC-ROM
decisions.reason: This is a substantive OCR/proofreading source-restoration and verified ca65 ROM-reconstruction workflow, not an ordinary original-source mirror.

decisions.title: fa8ntomas/blck-game-engine
decisions.reason: Although the README is only a title, the repository's primary engine.asm is a substantial project-specific annotated 6502 disassembly of Bruce Lee and Atari hardware behavior; unknown build/provenance facts remain explicitly unknown.

decisions.title: milnak/atari-vcs-disassembly
decisions.reason: The root is an aggregate of game sources and submodules, including credited third-party work, rather than one independently authored reconstruction. Individual canonical components require separate deduplication and review.

decisions.title: Dalekamistoso/MSXDUMPTOOLS
decisions.reason: The repository is a redistribution bundle of separately authored MSX utilities and assigns rights to their respective owners; it is useful as a discovery node but not a distinct development project.

decisions.title: radareorg/radare2

decisions.title: fcambus/jsemu

decisions.title: VelocityRa/awesome-game-file-format-reversing
decisions.reason: Large curated game-format/resource index; useful as a source, not a standalone analysis tool.

decisions.title: alfishe/amiga-bootcamp

decisions.title: sf2000-qpsx-playstation-emulator

decisions.title: alphaSeclab/awesome-reverse-engineering

decisions.title: danluu/debugging-stories

decisions.title: Two9A/c64clicker

decisions.title: pong-wars

decisions.title: ZX-spectrum-512K-cartridge-Droy-

decisions.title: Amiga ASM Development Workflow

decisions.title: Retrodev
decisions.reason: Integrated CPC development environment with bitmap/tile/sprite/map conversion, palette solving, RASM builds, scriptable exports and timing-validated Z80 raster-handler generation. README marks CPC/CPC+ supported while Spectrum, C64 and MSX are only prepared for; do not advertise those planned targets as implemented.

decisions.title: Slotshot

README states its PyCo compiler remains private and generated assembly/PRG/D64 outputs are not in this repository; public reproducible compilation is therefore unverified, despite documented play controls and runtime instructions.

decisions.title: Outrun 2026
decisions.reason: Released CPC 6128 fan conversion based on Master System OutRun. Michel Louvet states Claude Code wrote a native Z80 engine and extraction/music tools, with measured tracks, scenery and handling and SN76489-to-AY music conversion. Author reports emulator and real-hardware testing. Inspected Outrun V0.8.zip contains only Outrun V0.8.dsk (194816 bytes); no source or patches were linked, so source availability/compilability and detailed architecture remain unverified. Claims of native rewriting and AI model identity are attributed to the author, not independently reproduced. Targeted public search checked the project and itch creator/profile links, Outrun/CPC/title and Michel Louvet/GitHub searches. No matching public source was found; the similarly named yonifra/outrun2026 repository is an unrelated HTML5 game.

decisions.title: FreeMiNT
decisions.reason: Primary README and kernel/documentation inventory establish ongoing community maintenance of the existing open-source MiNT system. Keep as a reference/source node, rather than a new reconstruction or substantial newly authored port under the source-map rule that routine open-source maintenance alone is not an independent catalogue addition.

This is distinct from the tracked BBC binary reconstruction and JavaScript path-tracing remake. substantial historical implementation; runtime unverified. README reports the author’s actual build time on an Acer laptop and says the program was tested using OpenGL 3.0. Compilable/runnable=true are upstream-only historical build/runtime claims. No local CMake/Qt build, gameplay or compatibility test was performed, and complete playability remains null. Rights: GPL-3.0-or-later (source header).

decisions.title: Oil's Well — Godot 4 remake
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Native Godot remake of Oil’s Well. Pipe movement/retraction, collisions, enemies, oil collection, score, lives and level transitions are implemented in GDScript; neither a screenshot-only mockup nor a guest-instruction wrapper. gameplay source present; completion unverified. project.godot declares Godot 4.3, a main-menu scene and autoloaded game/music managers. Those settings and populated level scenes support the implementation scope, but no build, export, runtime or full-game test was performed. Every build flag stays null. Rights: No declared license found in inspected repository.

decisions.title: Knight of Wor — JavaFX remake of Wizard of Wor
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Native Java/JavaFX remake of the C64 Wizard of Wor subject, with maze, player/enemy, bullet, score/lives and timed-update logic. It is distinct from the existing C64 assembly reconstruction. implemented game source; runtime unverified. README documents mvn clean install; pom.xml targets Java 8, an executable TitleScreen entry and 0.0.1-SNAPSHOT. Tests exist but were not run. Instructions and an executable-JAR configuration do not establish a successful build or modern JavaFX compatibility; all build flags remain null. Rights: GPL-3.0.

decisions.title: Blok Copy RX — native C64 Remix Edition source
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Author-credited native homebrew source for the C64 Remix Edition, with VIC-II, joystick, title/game, score and puzzle-shuffling implementation. Source preservation does not by itself establish source restoration or binary-derived reverse engineering, so work_kinds is empty. It shares the Blok Copy design with the separate Atari edition. released source and binaries present. Source headers describe ACME assembly and Exomizer release packing; build.bat implements that recipe and PRG/binary assets are present. No successful clean assembly, execution or playability was independently established, and binary presence alone is insufficient; all build flags remain null. Rights: No declared license found.

decisions.title: Blok Copy — native Atari 8-bit Edition source
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Hardware-specific Atari edition of the shared Blok Copy homebrew design. Native display lists, interrupts, player/missile graphics and puzzle rules distinguish it from the C64 implementation. No predecessor binary is shown as reverse-engineering input; work_kinds is empty rather than inventing a source-restoration or RE-derived-port method. released source and binaries present. Source headers and build.bat provide Xasm assembly followed by Exomizer Atari packing, and OBX/XEX outputs are present. These establish a substantive source/build tree, not a verified clean build or playable release; all build flags remain null. Rights: No declared license found.

decisions.title: Ultima V Remastered — C64 cartridge/disk adaptation and patches
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Game-specific native C64 adaptation with loader/IO replacement, selective original music/IO disassembly, binary patches, savegame editor and build tooling. This is not a whole-game decompilation or rewrite. EasyFlash, 1581 and BackBit identify storage/device variants, not additional source platforms. author reports completed playthrough; independent runtime unverified. README says the author completed the EasyFlash version but did not test it thoroughly. Runnable/playable=true are upstream-only claims scoped to that variant, not independent verification of all media outputs. The Makefile assembles loaders, selectively disassembles original routines, patches disk data and packs media; compilable stays null pending a reproduced build with user-supplied disks. Rights: Apache-2.0 for new code.

decisions.title: 1NVADER — original C64 assembly game source
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Original native homebrew game source written in 2019, with C64 screen, sprites, joystick and gameplay initialization. No historical executable is being disassembled or reimplemented; source_platforms/source_cpu/work_kinds are empty. released 2019, source available. README explicitly says the game was assembled with TurboMacroPro and first distributed on 17 May 2019. Compilable=true is an upstream-only historical assembly claim, not a verified current build. The checked Makefile instead uses TMPx, Exomizer and c1541 to create a D64. Runtime/playability and byte identity remain unknown. Rights: GPL-3.0.

decisions.title: Destiny Hunter — PET homebrew with C64 and Apple II ports
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Standalone 2021 tribute homebrew with native game/map/enemy/control code and a stage editor. PET and C64 binaries are documented; Apple II branches and controls establish source support. This is one cross-platform original game, not a reconstruction of a predecessor commercial binary; source fields and work_kinds stay empty. released PET/C64 builds; additional target support partial. README documents PET/C64 release PRGs, a complete package and detailed gameplay/controls for a short self-contained game. Runnable/playable=true are upstream-only PET/C64 release claims. Apple II is source-supported only. Manual core.h target selection and machine-relative compiler paths remain; no clean compilation or game execution was performed, so compilable is null. Rights: Apache-2.0 (explicit file notice).

decisions.title: Wolf64 — native C64 Wolfenstein 3D fan port
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Native C64 Wolfenstein 3D fan implementation with assembly raycaster, enemy chase/shoot/line-of-sight logic and native VIC/SID/input/loader modules. It is distinct from the existing Amiga CD32 port and does not execute the DOS program through a guest CPU interpreter. active native port; version 1.9 identified in credits. README/build.sh give an ACME/Python/c1541 recipe for KERNAL and Krill disk variants; credits identify version 1.9. A version label and recipe do not establish a successful build, frame-rate measurement or tested complete game. No source build or C64/emulator execution was performed, so all build flags remain null. Rights: No general code license found; noncommercial/fan notice and third-party caveats.

decisions.title: Crazee Rider — original BBC Micro source
decisions.reason: Author-released source adapted for BeebAsm; upstream build recipe available Kevin Edwards identifies this as his original 1987 racing game, detokenized from BBC BASIC inline assembly and adapted to BeebAsm. ROUT1.6502 implements input, game-state reset and vehicle control; MODULE.6502 contains BBC hardware IRQ and palette writes. Master.mak assembles separate game modules and emits the SSD image. The BBC and Electron roots are authentic machine-specific source versions, not duplicated mirrors. The BBC code includes raster palette changes absent from the Electron implementation. Author publishes converted original source for preservation; no explicit reuse license or LICENSE file was found. Public availability does not establish open-source permission. Documented build uses BeebAsm and a Windows make.bat wrapper. Supplied assembly, binary data and disk templates were inspected; no build, byte comparison, emulator or hardware execution was performed. Windows path/case assumptions should not be interpreted as a portable Unix build. This root covers BBC Micro only. The historical introduction mentions Master 128 and Electron, but that does not establish their source is included here.

decisions.title: Crazee Rider — original Acorn Electron source
decisions.reason: Author-released Electron version with documented BeebAsm build Distinct original Electron release adapted by Kevin Edwards, retaining 6502 gameplay and rendering source. MODULE.asm has Electron-specific joystick sampling and omits the BBC raster-palette IRQ path; game-state/control source differs from the BBC root. README documents fewer simultaneous opponents and manual palette selection. Master.mak and make.bat target CrazeeRiderElectron.ssd. Author publishes converted original source for preservation; no explicit reuse license or LICENSE file was found. Public availability does not establish open-source permission. Documented build uses BeebAsm and a Windows make.bat wrapper. Supplied assembly, binary data and disk templates were inspected; no build, byte comparison, emulator or hardware execution was performed. Windows path/case assumptions should not be interpreted as a portable Unix build. Gameplay runs at a different speed on BBC hardware according to the author; preserve the Electron target rather than treating the related BBC implementation as the same machine build.

PATT.asm contains native alien-pattern state and sequencing logic; Master.mak assembles aliens, bombs, sprite drawing, sound, waves and pattern data, then packages the disk image. The BBC build uses MODE 2; its separate Electron counterpart uses different graphics and sound routines. Author publishes converted original source for preservation; no explicit reuse license or LICENSE file was found. Public availability does not establish open-source permission. Supplied assembly, binary data and disk templates were inspected; no build, byte comparison, emulator or hardware execution was performed. This root does not include a separately supported Master 128 release.

decisions.reason: Author-released distinct Electron source with BeebAsm recipe Original Electron version is preserved separately from the BBC Micro root. PATT.asm and SPRITES.asm contain concrete 6502 behavior and rendering; Master.mak selects the Electron code/data and loader. README explains MODE 5 four-color rendering, single-channel music and Plus 1/First Byte joystick support, providing machine-specific distinction from the BBC release. Author publishes converted original source for preservation; no explicit reuse license or LICENSE file was found. Public availability does not establish open-source permission. The author warns that this version runs unusually fast on a BBC Micro; machine support is not inferred from emulator loadability.

decisions.reason: Author-released source; anniversary title-screen modification Kevin Edwards released the sequel source for the BBC Micro anniversary; the original BBC BASIC source and converted assembly coexist. Main.asm and Object1.asm contain native game control/object initialization. Master.mak assembles gameplay modules and packages graphics and loader data. README explains MODE 5 as the memory-saving basis for bosses, pickups and other additions relative to Galaforce. Author publishes converted original source for preservation; no explicit reuse license or LICENSE file was found. Public availability does not establish open-source permission. Supplied assembly, binary data and disk templates were inspected; no build, byte comparison, emulator or hardware execution was performed. Windows path/case assumptions should not be interpreted as a portable Unix build. Module filename case and Windows path conventions need attention on a case-sensitive build host.

decisions.title: EDAS 1.8 — recovered C128 editor/assembler
decisions.reason: Recovered original self-hosting source; incomplete user documentation Mike Webb’s circa-1988 C128 editor/assembler, recovered by Kevin Edwards, includes both tokenized native source and a 168 KB readable assembly conversion. The assembly contains editor, parser/assembler and output routines, including C128 bank switching. It is substantive original development-tool source. README specifies self-building with supplied a1.8.prg on a C128 or emulator; creating a disk image and loading tokenized source are required. No explicit source license found; recovery/preservation credit is not a reuse grant. Self-hosted build requires the preassembled tool and .src input. The readable .asm file is for inspection and is not claimed to build using a modern cross-assembler. Documentation is explicitly incomplete. Historical NES and C64 development usage does not mean this editor runs on those machines; C128 is the runtime target.

decisions.title: wav2cas — MSX cassette audio and CAS toolkit
decisions.reason: Implemented cassette converter/synthesizer with embedded tests Pure-Python FSK demodulation and CAS encoding, with adaptive timing/confidence handling and optional ffmpeg conversion; adjacent scripts generate cassette audio and model recording/playback effects. Reviewed decode(), write_cas(), CAS synthesis and cassette DSP implementation; synthetic regression tests are present in source but were not run. This is a distinct MSX audio/CAS tool, rather than another copy of the already tracked PC-88 dwimsy tool. MSX-like is a format claim, not verified support for every retro computer. Default input conversion may use ffmpeg; pure-Python FLAC fallback is documented as slow. Root LICENSE is MIT, while cas2wav.py carries a separate public-domain assertion tied to its AI generation. Record the mixed notices without endorsing the claim that AI authorship automatically resolves rights. Tests and accuracy are upstream assertions/source facilities; no audio recovery or physical cassette test performed.

decisions.title: FAT8 D88 extractor and RBYTE tools
decisions.reason: Working according to upstream with heuristic detection and incomplete format coverage D88 FAT8 extraction implements sector/metadata/FAT-chain analysis and file reconstruction, plus protected-BASIC-save deobfuscation and character conversion. Concrete known-format structures cover PC-6001 mkII, PC-6601/SR, PC-88, PC-98 and Pasopia geometries. RBYTE image decoder code is also present. Distinct disk/filesystem utility from dwimsy’s currently implemented tape path; dwimsy only references this backend for broader integrations. README reports testing only a handful of images; machine detection is heuristic. BASIC detokenization, additional character sets and PC-6001 autostart detection remain TODO. rbyte88.py states that format details were inferred from one game and may be wrong. Root MIT license does not confer rights to input game images. PC-6001 mkII, PC-6601 and Pasopia are genuine extra machines needing catalogue-label review, not aliases for PC-88. Keep variant details in notes unless a new label is approved.

decisions.title: NONTAMA / MSX M-loader tape unpackers
decisions.reason: Implemented game-loader decoding with cartridge-builder support nontama_to_bload.py recognizes PC-6001 mkII NONTAMA headers, decodes loader payloads, and emits BLOAD data; mload_to_bload.py separately handles MSX Hudson/Honeybee loader tapes. mkrom.py generates native Z80 cartridge loader/trampoline bytes for the Warrior cartridge family using decoded data. README lists successful examples; implementation includes detailed analysis of an originally corrupted tape payload and charset smoke tests. PC-6001 mkII is a distinct hardware label that must be resolved before publication; do not relabel it PC-8001. Needs user-supplied P6/P6T or CAS images. MIT tool licensing does not license the games. Compatibility examples and cartridge-register fixes are upstream evidence only. A recent commit explains using port 0x7F for real hardware and PC6001VX compatibility; no cartridge/hardware validation was done.

decisions.title: cas2uef — compact CAS to BBC tape-image conversion
decisions.reason: Narrow format converter; deliberately heuristic tape timing Python converter splits compact CAS carrier blocks and writes UEF 0.10 data/tone/gap records for BBC Model B tape recordings. Actual serialization uses UEF headers and chunks, with a dummy starting block for older BBC OS behavior. Requires compact nonpadded CAS preserving block boundaries, specifically the form produced by DumpListEditor; this is not a general MSX-game-to-BBC port. CAS has lost waveform timing, so generated UEF uses heuristic pauses/default timings and is not audio-archival quality. README only says output appears to work in BeebEm. The script overwrites the named destination file. MIT applies to the converter, not its input tapes.

decisions.title: bin2fds — FDSStick capture-to-disk-image converter
decisions.reason: Narrow Python 2 converter; upstream describes limited success Parses FDS disk blocks and Nintendo-HVC headers from BIN captures, computes CRC diagnostics and emits an FDS header with padded 65,500-byte sides. Handles multiple input sides and rejects an existing output path; substantive recovery implementation rather than a file-extension renamer. Requires legacy Python 2, not Python 3. README says it only sometimes converts captures that other tooling failed to preserve. Code diagnoses CRC mismatches and can skip unexpected data; this is not proof of exact or complete recovery. Test against known-good source data before relying on an output. MIT license covers the tool, not original game disk contents. No input image was decoded during this review.

decisions.title: mzm2met — embedded NES ROM extraction
decisions.reason: Implemented bounded ROM decompressor/extractor with version-specific recipes mzm2met() decompresses headerless SZS data, apply_lzss_ofss() patches LZSS-compressed regions, and the output explicitly receives an iNES header. README gives offsets and input hashes for three 8 MiB MZM variants. Tool execution requires the user-supplied source image and correct per-version ranges. Primary documentation uses the acronym MZM rather than a full commercial title; the record does not expand it or assert an unsupported source-host machine. Version/offset-specific extraction is not an engine reconstruction or game-specific emulation runtime. Code has bounds checks but no independently verified output hash. MIT applies to tool code only. Supplied ROM recipes do not grant input or extracted-game redistribution rights.

decisions.title: kevedwards/timgeofffollinmusicdevdiskarchive
decisions.reason: README explicitly identifies this as a second recovery pass on the same Tim/Geoff Follin Einstein music-development disks previously recovered in already tracked breakintoprogram/archive-follin. Adds repaired/damaged data, raw IMG/DSK images, disk photos and K-prefixed newly archived disks; record as an alternate/additional preservation source rather than a second musical-driver project.

decisions.title: guybrush-atari/sonic-ste
decisions.reason: Tree has only .gitignore, README.md and Sonic-STe-0.8-alpha.zip; no primary implementation/build source inspected. The ZIP was not downloaded or executed, so do not assert its contents are binary-only.

decisions.reason: Legacy AtariLegend public website and CPANEL PHP/MySQL control-panel implementation, not Atari hardware/software reconstruction, original native retro code, a game port or emulation tool.

decisions.title: SG1000 multicart (xrip)
decisions.reason: README explicitly says heavily based on already tracked aotta/SD-1000 and uses its PCB. Firmware/menu changes are real, but retain as derivative lineage rather than inflate independent project count.

decisions.reason: README calls it a Lords of Conquest remake and says it remains unfinished. No substantive playable rules implementation is established by the inspected map/click scaffold.

decisions.title: Augmentinel
decisions.reason: README explicitly states the original gameplay runs by emulating the Spectrum version of The Sentinel. Spectrum.cpp accesses original game's memory addresses; repository contains Z80 core, Spectrum ROM and game snapshot, while C++/D3D11 supplies modern rendering/VR. Visual Studio 2019+ build and GPLv3 source license are documented. Game-specific original-CPU emulation is audit-only under current scope; do not promote as a native reimplementation.

decisions.reason: Historical prerelease disk and binary archive, with photos and exported executable files; no substantive newly reconstructed implementation or recovered editable game source identified in the inspected tree. Useful preservation source, not another Exile implementation. Retain as a preservation source; editable recovered implementation evidence needs further inspection before any project promotion.

decisions.title: f-fix/pc88_tape_tools
decisions.reason: Substantive PC-8001/PC-8801 tape implementation, but already tracked dwimsy explicitly extracts/refactors this core and keeps it as its verification baseline. Retain as upstream provenance rather than add another same-core record in this batch. Direct README AI attribution belongs to this upstream and should not be automatically copied to all dwimsy code.

decisions.reason: Only CPC setup/title/display and an empty gameplay self-jump are implemented. Retain the inspected evidence as a lead, not a native-game candidate. This applies the same threshold as Conquest.

decisions.title: Dinozorus — original Amiga television-game source
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Author-published source of the 1992–93 ATV television game, credited to Uğur “vigo” Özyılmazel. The repository’s later repair/import dates do not date the original game or an independent reverse-engineering effort. GPL-3.0 is present; graphics, characters, music and PRORUNNER have separately named contributors whose rights are not independently established. The README reports that the ADFs booted in FS-UAE after a 24-April-2022 fix and offers the level-1 binary to run and play. runnable/playable=true record those upstream historical claims only. The 2015 compilable-source statement is scoped to one transition level, so whole-repository compilable stays null. Asm-Pro and a locally edited dh1: include path are required; no present-day build was attempted.

decisions.title: Icarus — native Amiga and Atari voxel engine
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Native Icarus engine/demo with ACE and separate Atari ikbd/SNDH/libcmini support. No predecessor game is identified as a reconstruction subject. No top-level engine/assets license was found; bundled dependency licensing cannot be applied to the whole repository. README explicitly names A3000, supporting the new exact catalogue label Amiga 3000. README documents make -f makefile_amiga and make -f makefile_atari with Bebbo/m68k-atari toolchains. The recipes depend on ACE, ikbd, SNDH and libcmini libraries and include absolute compiler paths. README says the engine works on the listed systems but gives no bounded successful build report for the inspected revision; all build flags remain null.

decisions.title: SDDDE — Amiga A1200 3D engine and map converters
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Native 3D engine by Rst7/CBSIE, with a PC engine/data converter and kd-tree/PVS generator. Windows denotes companion output, not evidence of a Windows release of the Amiga demo. No project license was found. The LOAD_SPYRO option and bundled map data have unresolved provenance, so asset originality or redistribution is not asserted. The README says target/ contains an Amiga binary and converted data and names Bartman’s VSCode toolchain. SDDDE/Makefile supplies a -m68020 ELF-to-Hunk recipe using Windows shell commands. Bundled output is not proof of reproducibility or a completed playtest; compilable, runnable and playable stay null.

decisions.title: R-PAGE — native Amiga adventure-game framework
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Framework from RESISTANCE, with Athanor 2 and other games cited as clients. MIT project license is explicit; miniz, Shrinkler, NRV2, ptreplay and ADPCM retain named upstream provenance and their own terms. It is supporting development infrastructure, not a reconstruction of any cited client game. README explicitly says the portable code builds on SAS/C, but this review found no bounded successful build/test report for the inspected revision. The framework opens AmigaOS libraries and is not itself a complete game. All four build fields remain null rather than treating the generic build badge or library source as a playtest.

decisions.title: Amiga Game Engine 0.4 — system-friendly graphics framework
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Repository code credits Pedro Gil Guirado / Balrog Soft and carries an MIT license. C2P, music and texture components require separate provenance attention. Treat the project as a native framework, not a game reconstruction or independent PowerPC engine. SAS/C SCOPTIONS and smakefile describe compiling/linking Engine and framebuffer, bitmap, sprite, input and music modules. No successful build log or current runtime report was established. The brief README compatibility statement does not prove compilability or complete-game playability; all build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Planar — native Amiga blitter and game framework
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Original Planar C framework by Lorenzo Di Gaetano, with separately sourced ptplayer integration. No project-wide license file was found in the inspected tree. The framework is supporting native development, and no legacy game reconstruction lineage is asserted. README documents vbcc plus Amiga NDK and a make workflow; Makefile also requires vasm and ptplayer. The source implements blits and double-buffered BOB handling, but the project is explicitly work in progress. Build recipe presence is not successful-build evidence; all flags remain null.

decisions.title: SAGE — high-end Amiga RTG game-engine library
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. SAGE is Fabrice Labrador’s native high-end Amiga library, with tutorials, demos, LibInclude and external PT-AHIPlay support. Documentation warns the API is in development. No project-wide license was found; external component terms cannot license SAGE as a whole. README documents SAS/C 6.5+ (author uses 6.59), vasm, external LibInclude headers/assigns and three library variants. Source makefile adds prebuilt PT-AHIPlay.o and compiles 68060/68080 modules. The documented recipe and shipped libraries do not establish an independently reproduced build or game playtest; flags remain null.

decisions.title: UIK — original AmigaOS user-interface object toolkit
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Original UIK object engine by Jean-Michel Forgeas, identified as a 1992 release; objbox.c bears a 1990 implementation date and README links contemporary coverage. Those dates identify original development/publication, not reverse-engineering start. No explicit license was found. This is an archival toolkit subject, not an independently reconstructed engine. Historical preferences build requires lib:uik.lib, Amiga libraries, includeg:, lci:, UC: and PR: assigns and locale tools. Repository includes library objects and examples, but a complete reproducible modern build was not established. Compilable/runnable/playable and byte_exact remain null.

decisions.title: Laser Chess — Amiga BASIC-derived browser port
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Explicit lineage: Mike Duppong’s 1987 Compute! Laser Chess, Tim Midkiff’s Amiga BASIC version, then this p5.js port. Supplied scans preserve the source relationship. This is source-derived translation, not an independent binary reverse-engineering project. No project license was found, and magazine-source/image rights remain distinct. README describes serving the directory locally and calls the historical RawGit page playable. That link was not verified operational, and the same README lists rotation, redraw, end-game, sound, scaling and laser-boundary TODOs. No current completed-game/runtime or compile claim is promoted; all flags remain null.

decisions.title: AmiGalaga — native Galaga reconstruction for PAL Amiga 500
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Native reconstruction of Galaga behaviors with extracted user-ROM graphics, flight scripts and sound; MAME measurements and a separate Z80 analysis model supply reference evidence. Third-party hackbar-galaga disassembly is referenced but deliberately not bundled. MIT covers repository code only. Namco revision-B ROMs are user supplied, and README explicitly prohibits distributing generated executable/ADF data containing proprietary Galaga assets. README documents executable/ADF production and reports that the game has run in emulation on A500 through A4000, with one-player play through GAME OVER. runnable/playable=true record those upstream claims, not an independent test. A reproducible build still requires user-supplied Namco revision-B galaga.zip, vasm/vlink, Python 3.13+, uv and xdftool; compilable remains null because this review did not reproduce or inspect a bounded successful build log. byte_exact is null.

decisions.title: GermZ — native four-player Amiga game and map editor
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Original Last Minute Creations game with code by KaiN, music/sound by Luc3k and graphics/levels by Softiron. MPL-2.0 covers code unless stated otherwise; res assets are separately CC BY-SA 4.0. ACE is a dependency, not a predecessor game being reconstructed. README specifies Bebbo/Bartman GCC, CMake, AmigaCMakeCrossToolchains and an ACE-based asset build. CMake provides conversion and native linking steps. The inspected docs are build instructions, not an independent or bounded current successful-build record; all build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Shalatuvaar / amiMelee — native Amiga hex-map game prototype
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Shalatuvaar retains the older amiMelee identity and uses an external ACE checkout. The Melee influence is a rules/design relationship, not evidence of a binary translation or a licensed implementation of another computer game. No project-wide license was found. The old makefile expects ../ace/ace, copies its prebuilt objects and contains host-specific path handling. README is only the old amiMelee name. Actual game.c implements map, camera, character and mouse interaction with TODOs; no full combat, successful build or complete-game claim is supported. All build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Villages — native Amiga tile-and-road strategy-game source
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Native Last Minute Creations game source using ACE. An MIT code license is present, but standalone asset provenance and complete release requirements are not documented in a README. No historical game reconstruction or specific predecessor lineage is asserted. src/makefile expects configured CC_FLAGS and ACE: objects and copies/rebuilds the ACE dependency. No README documents a complete release/build flow; implementation has scoring/traversal logic and TODOs. Source presence is not proof of successful compile or finished gameplay, so all flags stay null.

decisions.title: WeegieNights — AmiBlitz Amiga Game Jam source
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Scottish Amiga Users Group 2022 jam entry with Rob Cranley code, named graphics/sound/level contributors and PHX ProTracker. Code is CC BY 4.0, other assets CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and Banjo Guy Ollie title music remains separately copyrighted and used with permission. Obtain the matching release assets; these terms do not collapse into one code license. README explicitly states the source was compiled using AmiBlitz 3.8 and 3.9, supporting compilable=true as an upstream report. It uses PHX ProTracker and separate release assets; the .ab3-only source checkout is not assumed self-contained. No independent compile or gameplay verification occurred; runnable/playable/byte_exact stay null.

decisions.title: FitzQuake Amiga 68k — AmiQuake-derived NovaMesa port
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Preserve FitzQuake → NovaCoder’s AmiQuake SDL base → this Amiga 68k/NovaMesa port. decisions.title: Tiny Pascal — C64 compiler and runtime port
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. C64 port and revival of the Chung/Yuen Tiny Pascal compiler, with BASIC compiler code, p-code generation and an implemented 6510 runtime/translator. The initial no-runtime statement is historical; current README/source establish subsequent runtime work. compiler.bas implements token/symbol tables and p-code generation, while runtime.asm contains implemented stack and I/O routines. process.sh invokes petcat/c1541 through a machine-specific VICE path. No compiler/runtime build or test program was executed, and planned file I/O and richer Pascal types remain incomplete; all build flags remain null. Preserve Chung and Yuen’s 1978 book/compiler provenance and Bill Fahle’s historical C64 port/revival. README says 1985/July 2026 whereas compiler.bas comments say 1984/June 2026, so no exact reconstruction-start date is chosen. MIT repository metadata does not erase historical attribution.

decisions.title: DraCopy and DraBrowse — Commodore file utilities
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Native Commodore file/disk copy and browser utilities, continued from Sascha Bader’s released source. The reviewed implementation performs concrete directory, file, disk and optional RAM-expansion operations; this is utility source development, not recovered game code. The custom permission requires original-source/author attribution and includes no warranty; no SPDX label is guessed.

decisions.title: C64 Studio / RetroDevStudio — C64 development IDE
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Linux support is through Wine/PlayOnLinux, not a native Linux GUI build. README reports success under PlayOnLinux/Ubuntu and testing under Linux Mint 21.3 with Wine, so runnable=true is an upstream-only compatibility-layer claim. Current csproj frameworks are net10.0-windows, net3.5 and net4.8; the README’s older .NET 6 binary list is not substituted for current project configuration. No compilation was performed. C64Studio repository and RetroDevStudio source namespace identify one continuing IDE project, not separate roots. Inspected license.md grants MIT for C64 Studio and lists separately licensed dependencies including LGPL-3.0; GitHub NOASSERTION does not replace the actual notices.

decisions.title: SMB1 transpiler — Apple II/C64 VERA port rebuilder
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. C99 ROM-to-disk rebuilder for an existing Apple II A2VERA/C64 VERA Super Mario Bros. port, combining positional game-code transformations, Super Mario All-Stars graphics conversion and embedded 6502 glue. It is not a general compiler, a stock-machine port or an original-source archive. README explicitly reports building and running both MinGW-w64 x86_64 and i686 builder executables, plus generated C64-image boot to the title screen. Compilable/runnable=true are upstream-only and scoped to those reports; full playability remains unknown. No candidate build, ROM processing, hardware test or byte comparison occurred. Disk/file checksum claims are not independent byte-exact evidence. This wrapper rebuilds the a2vera port using generated a2vera_blobs.h; the assembler/source pipeline lives elsewhere. Adrian Black’s controller code is MIT, Krill Loader v166 is BSD-3-Clause, and Joe Burks’s A2VERA hardware is separately credited. Main code is PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, explicitly not OSI open source. Nintendo ROMs/game art/code and generated disk images receive no license grant; upstream says not to redistribute the outputs.

The actual Python parser supports listing/extraction, with a focused README. decisions.title: Reblitz64 — reconstructed Blitz! BASIC compiler
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Structured-source reconstruction and JavaScript port of the Blitz!/Austro-Speed C64 BASIC V2 compiler. Original BASIC control flow was rewritten and transpiled, with assembly helpers replaced in JavaScript; the main output does not execute a guest 6502 interpreter. README links a live browser compiler, documents Node invocation and reports a measured compiler benchmark, so runnable=true is an upstream-only compiler report. Regeneration uses petcat, basictransplr, js-beautify, Perl and shell scripts, none run here. The incomplete regex-dependent transpiler can alter FOR-loop semantics; compilation/output correctness and byte identity remain unverified. Preserve Blitz!/Austro-Speed compiler provenance, the separately compared blitz 0.1 emulator port, the author’s basictransplr helper and CrankThePRINT rendering tool. The helper is not a general semantics-preserving transpiler. No repository-wide license was found.

decisions.title: C64 KERNAL and BASIC — ASM6502 source port
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Assembler-source port of preserved Commodore KERNAL V3 and BASIC V2 source from mist64/cbmsrc, with layout/ROM patches and a checksum helper. The contribution is modern assembler adaptation and reproducible-ROM tooling, not independently recovered or binary-decompiled original source. README supplies assembly, split-ROM layout, checksum patching and MD5 verification commands, with flags that change replica behavior. Commands and reference hashes are recipes, not reproduced builds. No ROM was assembled, patched or compared, so all build flags remain null. Explicit predecessor: https://github.com/mist64/cbmsrc, already represented in the discovery-source index as github-mist64-cbmsrc, not an existing project record. Preserve that original-source lineage and the distinct ASM6502 conversion contribution. kernal/disclaim.a65 retains Commodore’s 1983 computer-use restrictions; cbmsum.c separately declares BSD-3. The entire repository must not be called BSD/open source.

decisions.title: rtl8139re.device — AmigaOS 4 driver reconstruction
decisions.reason: Repository describes reverse-engineered C reconstruction of Hyperion rtl8139.device; native SANA-II resident driver implements PCI enumeration, transmit handling and now IRQ/RX infrastructure. Makefile cross-compiles ppc-amigaos-gcc with -mcpu=440; target is AmigaOS 4 on QEMU sam460ex, with real Sam460ex/AmigaOne hardware only expected. Latest history documents Roadshow packet/copy-hook debugging and an RX rollback, so README pending-status table is stale relative to source. Incomplete driver: latest commit rolls back RX-side CallHookPkt dispatch; no claim of working full TCP/IP or production readiness. License explicitly TBD. Real-hardware compatibility is unverified; QEMU reports are upstream-only. PPC build flags identify target ISA, not 68k Amiga compatibility or minimum RAM.

decisions.title: Pinball Illusions — browser reconstruction
decisions.reason: Independent TypeScript browser reconstruction of the 1995 four-disk Amiga AGA release, with N-ball fixed-point simulation, collision maps, table mission-bytecode interpreter, canvas rendering and audio. Inspected ball-physics.ts and package.json show real implementation and Node/TypeScript build/test scripts; no 68k runtime wrapper is required. Original AGA release has three tables in this project; PC/console-exclusive Vikings is intentionally excluded. Inspected mode-vm.ts explicitly leaves eight mission opcodes unimplemented and deliberately ends missions when the ball ends, diverging from original behavior. This is not full gameplay parity. Upstream gameplay/parity/test counts are not independently validated and README explicitly retains contact-frame physics and sprite/collision alignment discrepancies. Ships disk-derived artwork, audio, music, geometry and mission data. Build rights gate requires PINBALL_ILLUSIONS_DERIVED_AUTHORIZED=1; this operator assertion is not evidence of redistribution permission. No repository license found. Re-extraction needs operator-owned original disks; clean-room description is upstream wording, not a legal conclusion.

decisions.title: Perihelion 2.0 — Amiga BBX game reconstruction
decisions.reason: Rebuilds Craig Dorrell’s Amiga BBX door game using surviving introduction, screenshots and original bitmap fonts; Python engine serves terminal and browser clients. Actual gameplay module implements movement, combat, economy, fleets and multiplayer state. Amiga-font parser recovers preserved glyphs into modern rendering assets. Historical README.TXT supports Amiga BBX origin; modern README.md carefully distinguishes surviving material from unavailable binary/full manual. No original game binary is available to this project: reconstruction includes inferred rules, naming choices, player recollections and modern additions, so it is not a binary-derived decompilation. No license found; original font/artwork is preserved rather than newly authored. Rights and full behavioral equivalence remain unverified. Repository description says 1988 while modern README specifically reconstructs the 1992 version 2.0; retain 1992 target and do not silently harmonize these dates.

decisions.title: ReFlood — native reconstruction of Amiga Flood
decisions.reason: C99/SDL2 native source reconstruction of Flood with game logic, asset extractor, audio/presentation, editor, deterministic test harness and experimental local split-screen mode. CMake defines a reusable flood_core and reflood/editor targets; src/game.c implements native gameplay rather than invoking an Amiga emulator. Only supported original IPF revision can be converted via disk-analyse and extracted; manifest checks reconstructed files. Original Flood data is not distributed in releases and is required for play and gameplay tests. Needs a legally obtained supported IPF plus disk-analyse with SPS/CAPS support. GPL-3.0 covers repository code; it does not license original assets. Multiplayer is experimental, editor cannot yet create/edit triggers. Latest editor-focus report explicitly lacks an XFCE/SDL runtime check. We did not build or run the game or editor.

decisions.title: Rog — C64 demo disassembly and extraction toolkit
decisions.reason: Preserves a C64 demo via generated/named 6502 assembly and Python graph-disassembly, bitmap/charset/sprite and SID extraction tools. Disassembler implements entry discovery, control-flow traversal, overlap/conflict tracking and I/O-register symbolization; sources are substantive rather than only a binary archive. Committed coverage report shows 2,674 instructions/7,184 decoded bytes out of a 46,911-byte payload (15.31%). Remaining data bytes are emitted to support rebuild; 15.31% coverage is not complete semantic reconstruction. README provides 64tass/cmp byte-rebuild instructions but does not establish our own successful comparison; byte_exact remains unknown. Original demo/SID/images are committed, with no license found. Disassembler opcode definitions acknowledge cc65 derivation.

decisions.title: LADS — reconstructed book-source assembler
decisions.reason: Reconstructs Richard Mansfield’s printed LADS assembler listings with OCR corrections, modern ca65 translation, machine/config overlays and object-code oracles. C64 generated source explicitly sets 6502 ISA and machine I/O equates; materialization scripts produce per-machine assembly/binary/disk artifacts. Root is substantive source reconstruction plus verification tooling; not simply a scanned-book archive. C64 VERIFY.txt reports 5,032 assembled bytes compared against a 4,986-byte oracle prefix, all matching. Do not call the entire binary byte-exact or independently verified. Disk images are documented as structurally validated but not emulator-boot-tested upstream. Apple from-source variant remains a study, with canonical decompiled variant retained. MIT applies only to original tools; reconstructed source/object code remains under original copyright. Raw book pages must be separately fetched.

decisions.title: virtnet.device — native AmigaOS 4 virtio network driver
decisions.reason: Native PowerPC SANA-II virtio-net-pci driver implementing legacy PCI transport, virtqueues, packet paths and Roadshow integration for AmigaOS 4.1. Source virtio.c implements I/O register access and device/queue setup; Makefile builds device.c plus virtio.c with ppc-amigaos-gcc. Upstream reports end-to-end TCP on QEMU sam460ex, approximately 24–25 Mbit/s with zero retransmissions in measured runs. Legacy/transitional virtio device supported; modern-only 0x1041 is not yet supported. Introductory multi-gigabit claims are generic aspirations; actual documented measurements are much lower and slower than the e1000 comparison. License says same as sibling virte1000 without a license file in this repository; licensing remains unresolved. Only QEMU testing is established upstream.

decisions.title: NetBSD rump — incomplete AmigaOS 4 network-stack port
decisions.reason: Substantive work-in-progress port provides PowerPC/AmigaOS adaptation for NetBSD rump kernel threads, memory, locks, timers and IPC, plus a socket-library shim architecture. Inspected osal_thread.c implements native Exec task creation/join and rump hypercall wrappers; fdtable.c deliberately provides an in-memory socket scaffold. Latest NEXT_STEPS.md supersedes stale README status: rump_init has been run, reaches about 15 adaptation-layer calls, then reproducibly faults in an OS4 library. Not a functioning TCP/IP stack. Real network dispatch, full BSD API and driver bridge are incomplete; documented deterministic DSI crash blocks initialization. Makefile/build reports prove only upstream partial compilation/symbol closure, not working networking. No local compilation or execution.
