CD32 is a conditional source option and is not claimed as a verified output here.

decisions.title: Ambermoon — original Amiga development-source snapshot
decisions.reason: Developer J. Horneman preserves a snapshot of Ambermoon 68000 assembly and contemporary data-format, design and localized-text documents. Selected MAIN.S and COMBAT.S contain real initialization, party-data handling, combat checks and combat-screen logic. README explicitly says the source is probably incomplete, probably not final, and cannot be transformed into a full game. Do not present it as a buildable release. README grants no license and says ownership of Thalion rights is unknown.

decisions.title: Habitat — original C64 client and Stratus server-source archive
decisions.reason: Museum restoration of the original Lucasfilm/QuantumLink Habitat archive contains the C64 macross client/art, Stratus VOS PL/I backend and historical tools/documents. Client Makefile invokes macross and slinky; comm_control.m implements actual host messages, region transitions and client response handling. Case-sensitive filesystem is required because some C64 source filenames differ only by case. README documents multiple source/binary vintages and missing tools including filldisk, loadrom and mtobin. Bundled binaries need not match nearby sources. C64 client depends on a compatible network/server environment; no modern server deployment or end-to-end playable setup was verified. Stratus VOS is archival backend context, not a newly claimed C64 runtime profile.

decisions.title: C64 SID players — recovered and disassembled music-driver sources
decisions.reason: Root collection of original and reverse-engineered C64 music players, including Rob Hubbard, Martin Galway and other named musicians. Selected Commando and Arkanoid assembly players contain driver implementation and music data; README aims to make each file produce a .sid using ACME. README warns some source may not assemble until cleaned up. No player was built or listened to. Repository MIT license is present, but ownership and permission for every historical player/tune were not independently established. A .sid output is consumed by a SID player; do not confuse host playback with a native full-game reconstruction.

decisions.title: CommLib2 — reconstructed C64 RS-232 communications library
decisions.reason: Reverse-engineered version of İlker Fıçıcılar’s CommLib2 RS-232 library with actual receive/transmit and setup assembly. Makefile uses KickAssembler through Docker and has c1541 disk-image packaging; README places code at $CA00 and receive buffer at $9000. BASIC users must reserve the receive buffer by reducing top-of-BASIC memory as documented; relocation is an upstream expectation, not verified. No license file was found in the inspected tree; original-library and reconstruction rights remain unclear.

decisions.title: skit — C64 emulator and reverse-engineering tool prototype
decisions.reason: C++ general C64 emulator/analysis project, rather than a wrapper dedicated to one game. Selected source constructs a 6510 CPU, 64 KiB RAM, BASIC/KERNAL/character ROMs, CIA and video devices; CPU source implements fetch, opcode execution, interrupt and debugging paths. Visual Studio 2010 project supplies Win32 configurations and SDL-related desktop build context. Upstream description calls it a slow C64 emulator intended to become a reverse-engineering tool. Completeness and timing accuracy were not independently tested. No root README or license was found. Bundled Commodore ROM images and third-party DLLs have separate unresolved redistribution rights.

decisions.title: mlxifier — C64 MLX II checksum-listing generator
decisions.reason: Small complete Rust command-line tool reimplementing Compute! MLX II checksums for C64 type-in listings. Source skips the two-byte PRG header, groups data into eight-byte blocks, zero-pads the final block and computes/emits address/data/checksum lines. No README or license file is present; arguments and usage were inferred from the inspected main function. Host Rust/Cargo utility, not native C64 code. No particular host OS support or checksum parity was tested.

decisions.title: Galactic Empire — native C64 game reconstruction in C
decisions.reason: C reconstruction of the original C64 Galactic Empire with actual galaxy generation, player/world/mission logic and graphics modules. Despite the Raspberry Pi name and metadata wording, the Makefile defaults to cc65 target c64 and builds a C64 executable; README describes running it in VICE on a Pi. Raspberry Pi is the emulator host, not the output ISA or a native ARM port. README names cc65 2.19 and VICE 3.5-era tooling. No license file was found and gameplay equivalence was not checked.

decisions.title: Blagger JS — C64 gameplay reconstruction for the browser
decisions.reason: Substantive JavaScript gameplay with player movement, collision, jump arcs, platforms, enemies, audio and canvas rendering; this is not a game-specific CPU emulator. Code labels movement rules with original 6502 addresses and distinguishes verified disassembly-derived behavior from tunable approximations; embedded assets identify a VICE snapshot as their source. The cited js/movement.md derivation file is not in the inspected two-file tree. Original data/assets are embedded and no license is present. Timing is explicitly described as not fully measured; source uses approximation/tuning notes. No runtime or fidelity test was performed.

decisions.title: AmigaED — Qt cross-development editor for Amiga software
decisions.reason: C++ Qt5/QScintilla cross-development editor with Amiga templates, vbcc/GCC selection and UAE startup integration. mainwindow.cpp implements compile/run and editor actions; qmake application.pro declares Qt widgets, print support and QScintilla dependencies. Experimental/example editor. README reports compiler failure for paths containing whitespace. BSD is only speculative upstream and is not included as supported. README uses a custom restricted public-domain-style statement with ideological use restrictions; Qt/QScintilla licenses apply separately. Do not summarize it as unrestricted public domain. This runs on modern host systems to create Amiga software; proposed AmigaOS4/AROS targets are roadmap items.

decisions.title: Supermon+64 — annotated source restoration and relocator reconstruction
decisions.reason: Jim Butterfield’s Supermon+64 machine-language monitor restored as heavily annotated 64tass source, with original archive/binary and a disassembled relocator. Makefile and Python builder create a relocated PRG from two fixed-address assemblies; source implements monitor, assembler/disassembler and memory/register operations. README claims an identical original binary; this is an upstream claim only and byte_exact stays unknown. Maintainer explicitly dedicates their comments/relocator work/builder to public domain, but describes original software’s public-domain status as best knowledge rather than a independently verified grant.

decisions.title: Freedroid Classic — high-level remake of C64 Paradroid
decisions.reason: Original Freedroid Classic is a C implementation of the C64 Paradroid game with extensions, distinct from the later Freedroid RPG spinoff. Inspected main loop and takeover implementation contain direct game logic; current configure.ac requires SDL3, SDL3_image and SDL3_mixer and provides Unix and MinGW/Cygwin branches. Current source dependencies are SDL3, not assumptions from older SDL1/SDL2 releases. Additional JPEG/PNG/zlib dependencies are checked in configure.ac. Historical Android settings exist but were not treated as proof of current Android support. No build or gameplay test performed.

decisions.title: C64 face generation — native PCA graphics demonstration
decisions.reason: BitCamp project and expanded version use C/cc65 to draw and interactively vary faces from five stored principal components on the C64. Host Python script derives components with scikit-learn PCA; the C program stores coefficient data and uses TGI graphics and hardware input. Training images are not included; Python preprocessing uses author-local absolute dataset paths. No license was found. The workload uses PCA; that alone is not evidence of AI-assisted development. Windows batch file points at a local cc65 installation; native runtime and any paddle/input requirements were not independently exercised.

decisions.title: ACEBasicJS — browser compiler and Amiga-inspired runtime
decisions.reason: New recursive-descent ACE BASIC-to-JavaScript compiler with browser runtime for Amiga-inspired screens/windows, input, graphics, sound, menus and turtle commands. Compiler explicitly treats C ACE as a reference specification; it emits JavaScript and does not emulate Amiga hardware. Source and static-server instructions are present. Compatibility is incremental and tied to documented seed programs, not full ACE/AmigaOS equivalence. No standalone license file was found in this repository; original ACE licensing should not automatically be copied to the new implementation.

decisions.title: ZGloom — high-level reimplementation of Amiga Gloom
decisions.reason: Canonical C++ reimplementation of Amiga Gloom with Zombie Massacre support, actual game logic/renderer and SDL2/SDL2_mixer/LibXMP build. Windows binary is documented as requiring VS2013 runtime; Linux instructions use the supplied Makefile. README lists incomplete HUD/menu, infinite lives, missing Defender subgame, sound issues and renderer discrepancies. Do not imply feature or timing parity. Upstream explicitly leaves its overall license unresolved and notes uncertainty over embedded game data and DeCrunchmania code. Original Gloom source grant excludes assets.

decisions.title: c64kit and c64lib — native C64 development framework
decisions.reason: Repository now contains a Python build/asset/testing toolkit plus substantial native 6502 assembly hardware/game helper modules. Selected VIC implementation manipulates video bank/charset/screen registers; Python/Makefile build pipeline assembles native C64 outputs. Historical PET code is explicitly archived outside the current build. README calls its Invaders demonstration complete, but inspected play-state code awards points on firing and simulates game over instead of full invader gameplay. Catalogue this as a development framework/prototype, not a verified complete game. No top-level license file was found. Build, tests and package outputs were not run. PET provenance does not establish a current PET target; current source explicitly says C64-only assembly.

decisions.title: GEOS KERNAL original TASS-era predecessor
decisions.reason: 1999 TASS-era predecessor by the same author as already-tracked c64-geos2000; source/provenance value retained, no duplicate project counted. The original README describes changed booter/byte layout and dependency on the remaining GEOS system; its 99%-identical wording is not byte-exact proof.

decisions.title: Original ACE 2.4 source-distribution provenance
decisions.reason: Original ACE 2.4 distribution is provenance for the already-tracked enhanced ACE compiler. It has GPL-era source and historical build scripts, but is not counted as another compiler identity. Browser ACEBasicJS is separate. Native ACE’s Workbench 1.3/2.x and 512 KiB statements are lineage-only requirements and do not apply to the separately counted browser ACEBasicJS.

decisions.title: c64-de mirror with unresolved original provenance
decisions.reason: README/image URLs and copyright identify mytechnotalent/Kevin Thomas lineage although GitHub marks this non-fork; claimed original repository returned 404. Hold mirror identity pending provenance. No byte-exact or asset-license claims accepted.

decisions.title: ZGloom macOS derivative and lineage evidence
decisions.reason: Substantive modern macOS variant of ZGloom, retained as related evidence rather than a second engine identity in this bounded batch. README declares AI-assisted coding and bundled game data; license defers upstream whose own licensing is unresolved. CMake uses bundled SDL2/libXMP and built-in mixer despite older README SDL2_mixer instructions. The duplicate decision groups this derivative under the canonical engine identity; it does not deny substantial independent port work. Apple Silicon/Intel/macOS and the AI badge belong to the derivative, not automatically to canonical ZGloom. No build or runtime was tested and no bundled-data redistribution rights were established.
